newsitem.title: USA: Texas molester who wanted castration sent to prison.
newsitem.headline: Texas molester who wanted castration sent to prison.

text.p: A convicted child molester who pleaded to be castrated to stop him from assaulting children again was found guilty on Tuesday in a second case and sentenced to 20 years in jail.
Larry Don McQuay, 33, was convicted in a trial that lasted just 16 minutes of three counts of indecency with a child arising from a 1989 assault on a nine-year-old girl.
"He's a fixated pedophile," Bexar County District Attorney Steven Hilbig told state district judge Terry McDonald.

McQuay made headlines in April 1996 by begging the state to castrate him when he was paroled from prison under mandatory release rules after serving six years for another 1989 assault in which he molested a six-year-old boy. He made a futile attempt to castrate himself with a razor blade.
McQuay said he had sexually molested scores of children and might end up killing one if he was left intact, but the state, for legal reasons, could not castrate him.
Victims' rights groups volunteered to pay for the procedure, but could not find a physician to perform it.
Under a law passed last month by the Texas legislature, McQuay, as a repeat sex offender, could now be castrated while in prison if he asks for it.
Under the terms of his 1996 parole, McQuay was kept in a private jail in San Antonio, but McDonald sent him immediately back to state prison on Tuesday.
"I want him transported to TDC (Texas Department of Corrections) on the next available bus," McDonald said. He called McQuay a "manipulator."

In the brief trial, McQuay pleaded not guilty to the charges, but neither side put on witnesses. Instead, under agreement by both sides, McDonald examined written evidence, then found McQuay guilty and gave him the maximum possible sentence.
